subject: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Hi Sarah —

Good to connect last week. As discussed, I’m opening a mutual action plan (MAP) thread so we can lock the evaluation milestones and a realistic activation window for Orion’s Dedicated/Private capacity. I sketched an initial timeline and a first-pass GPU pool sizing model attached. Key questions we need to agree on quickly: 

- Evaluation acceptance criteria and signoff owner
- Preferred deployment mode (Dedicated hosted pool vs Private VPC / on-prem)
- Target PO/commitment date and activation window (we need these to reserve hardware)

High-level guidance up front (so you can weigh options):
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool): typical lead time to reserve and place H100-backed capacity ~ 6–8 weeks from signed PO for standard regions; shorter if we use reserved burst capacity.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): lead time varies by model and on-prem procurement — expect 10–14 weeks for full on-prem H100 delivery + installation; VPC private instances ~8–12 weeks depending on cloud region quota.
- If you’re flexible on quantization and model family we can reduce capacity needs by 20–40% (lower peak GPU counts).

I attached: MAP_Orion_v0.1.xlsx (mutual action plan draft), GPU_Pool_Sizing_Model.csv (first-pass numbers), Redwood_SLA_Draft.pdf (shows SLA options tied to Dedicated commitments).

Can you confirm who at Orion will be the formal eval approver and whether procurement needs a separate thread? Once we have that, I’ll convert the MAP to a tracked HubSpot document and share a DocuSign for the PO + SLA.

Proposed milestones (placeholder):
1) Eval kickoff & dataset handover — Aug 28
2) Eval signoff — Sep 15
3) PO issued — Oct 1
4) Capacity activation (Dedicated) — Nov 15

If you prefer a later activation we can stagger tranches; I wanted to give a firm example so you can scope procurement. 

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha.k@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Neha —

Thanks, that outline is helpful. Procurement is cc’d here (procurement@oriontx.com) — they’ll need the MAP and the SLA draft for internal review. Quick answers:

- Eval approver: myself + Dr. Miguel Alvarez (cc’d on our side)
- Deployment preference: we favor a VPC/private option (data residency + compliance). If that drives >10 week lead time, we may accept a hybrid approach (initial Dedicated tranche to unblock product work, full Private later).

Can you add a row in the MAP that models a hybrid plan (initial 2-month Dedicated tranche followed by Private handoff)? Also we’ll need your SOC 2 report and encryption/KMS details for the security review.

Sarah Jensen
Head of ML Platforms | Orion Therapeutics
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>, Orion Procurement <procurement@oriontx.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Sarah —

Attached I updated the MAP to include a hybrid scenario (tab: HybridTranche). Summary of the two-lane approach:

- Tranche A (Dedicated): 8 H100-equivalent slots for 8 weeks — spin-up target 6–8 weeks post-PO. Purpose: unblock integration, run dev evals and latency benchmarks.
- Tranche B (Private VPC): 24 H100-equivalent slots full capacity — procurement & region quotas typically target 10–14 weeks after PO for VPC + cloud quota adjustments.

Security evidence: SOC 2 PDF and KMS integration notes are included in the Redwood_SLA_Draft.pdf. If your security team needs a more formal package I’ll loop our security lead.

A few engineering notes on sizing (also in GPU_Pool_Sizing_Model.csv):
- We assumed 1.2x headroom for model token peaks and 20% overhead for KV cache retention.
- If you enable 8-bit quantization for dev traffic we estimate required H100s reduce ~30% for generation-heavy workloads.

Next asks for Orion to confirm:
1) Eval acceptance criteria owner (confirm Dr. Alvarez?)
2) Which regions you want for the Private tranche (us-west-2 or eu-west-1? — affects lead times)
3) Procurement timeline target for PO issuance

I’ll also create a HubSpot MAP record (HUB-23456) and drop in the attachments so procurement can pull from one place.

Thanks,
Neha
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>, Orion Procurement <procurement@oriontx.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Quick technical notes / suggestions —

Neha / Sarah: I updated the sizing sheet with two alternate profiles (tab: QuantizedProfile, tab: MixedModelProfile). High level:
- If Orion can accept a small model family change for latency-critical endpoints (move from 70B dense to 70B q4_0 or a 30B optimized family), we can reduce concurrent GPU requirement by ~35%.
- For the hybrid: recommend we stage traffic routing so the Dedicated tranche handles 100% of dev/test traffic and 20% of production traffic for the first 6 weeks; then cutover as Private tranche becomes available.

Operational constraints to flag to procurement:
- Private VPC requires cloud quota increases which are region-dependent — I recommend us-west-2 for fastest turnaround in our experience.
- DocuSign template: I added a pre-fill DocuSign link in the Drive folder for a PO + SLA with 30-day acceptance windows.

Link to updated model: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Orion-MAP-Working
HubSpot deal: HUB-23456

-Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orion Procurement <procurement@oriontx.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Neha / Karthik —

Thanks for the updates. We reviewed the hybrid plan with our ML infra team and procurement. A few clarifications / asks before we proceed:

1) Please share your most recent SOC 2 Type II report and the KMS public integration doc (for our compliance packet).
2) Procurement requests an initial draft redline of the PO timeline (we prefer PO by Oct 15, activation tranche A by Dec 1 if PO by Oct 15).
3) We’d like the MAP to include a contingency clause if Private tranche lead times exceed 14 weeks — auto-scale Dedicated burst for the first 12 weeks.

We’re comfortable with the eval approver set (Dr. Miguel Alvarez). I’ll ask procurement to aim for an internal decision window by Oct 3.

Sarah
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@oriontx.com>, Orion Procurement <procurement@oriontx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Aug 2025 17:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment-stitch MAP & activation window for GPU pool

Sarah / team —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Action items and next steps I’m committing to: 

1) Attach SOC 2 Type II and expanded KMS notes to the HubSpot MAP record by EOD tomorrow (we’ll include a security point-of-contact).
2) Update MAP to reflect: PO target Oct 15, Dedicated tranche A activation target Dec 1 (if PO by Oct 15), and the contingency auto-scale clause (Dedicated burst for first 12 weeks) — will send v0.2 for redline by Fri Aug 29.
3) Open a DocuSign PO + SLA draft for procurement pre-review (link in HubSpot / Drive).
4) Schedule weekly check-ins starting Sep 1 — propose Mondays 10:00am PT for 30 mins.

If this captures everything, I’ll move the MAP to HubSpot (HUB-23456) and send the DocuSign pre-fill to procurement. Please confirm the procurement contact for signature routing.

Thanks —
Neha
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha.k@redwood.ai
